name: closer-to-the-original-loop
style: late-90s New York street rap, one heavyset MC going down his rules like a checklist read across a kitchen table: the rule, one plain clause of reasoning, then he stops; level, conversational, unhurried, each line given its whole bar with empty space after it, a deliberate beat of silence right before each punchline lands. Vocal: enormous man, low velvet chest baritone, lazy Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze audible on every inhale, dry and right on the mic. Instrumental: 89 BPM, hard sparse boom-bap drums, thick knocking kick, hard flat snare, long gaps between hits; the loop is one brief crying jazz-guitar slide lifted from a 1977 jazz LP, chopped and repeated every bar, cold minor menace; the Rhodes-and-organ figure buried deep beneath as a dim held pad, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; before every rule a separate rough hollering voice cut from an old vinyl record stabs in alone like a scratch to bark the number, then silence before the MC replies; bare, almost empty, no hook, no singing
exclude: singing, sung chorus, melodic hook, female vocals, double-time flow, rapid-fire delivery, autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 slides, bright synths
lyrics:
[Intro: lone guitar-slide loop, then the MC, calm and level]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Rule 1]
[sampled shout]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Rule 2]
[sampled shout]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Rule 3]
[sampled shout]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Rule 4]
[sampled shout]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Rule 5]
[sampled shout]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Rule 6]
[sampled shout]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Rule 7]
[sampled shout]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Rule 8]
[sampled shout]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Rule 9]
[sampled shout]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Rule 10]
[sampled shout]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro: drums cut, guitar slide alone, MC plain and slow]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End: loop plays out]
